title: Drive Away Dolls(2024) & The Burden of Expectations

commenti.body: I personally enjoyed the movie. I knew it wasn't going to be the best thing from them since it is only made by Ethan. But as a whole, it is a good homage to the B-movies with good charms between the characters, dialogue and humor used. Sure, it is not perfect and I wish it was a bit longer. But for what it is, it's a perfect entertaining B-movie vibe.

I liked that it was only 90 minutes, but I did get the feeling that it could have used “more” to feel like it actually had a point. It’s an incredibly pointless phallus—er—I mean movie.

I loved how stupid it was though. The bit where >!the drive-away clerk was watching the flashlight beam and throws the paper up!< is the type of absolutely useless gag that kill me.

Love the Coen brothers and was excited to see Ethan Coen venture out on his own for this road-trip comedy.

The film is well made, well shot, for the most part has good performances (with one notable exception, see below), and is short and sweet at 84 minutes. All good things.

But I didn't care for this film. Won't go as far as to say I hated it, but it is below the ok line. It's a comedy where many of the jokes just do not land. Some bits are pretty funny, but you could tell there were other intended funny moments that weren't funny.

The biggest problem in the movie is that Margaret Qualley's character, Jamie, is irritating and grating. Qualley puts on the absolute worst Southern/Texas accent I've ever heard and it really takes me out of this movie. Whether it was on purpose or not (I'm sure some people defending this movie will claim it was intentional), it's still god awful and ruins the film. As alluded to above, it's a shame because the rest of the cast is really good.

I really wanted to like this film, but it's just not good enough for what it was setting out to do. I'm sure some people will love it just for its LGBTQ representation, and that's fine, but if you want a LGBTQ comedy that extremely funny from beginning to end, go watch Bottoms (Which I do recommend for all!), which is currently on Amazon Prime in the US.

Sadly, this is skippable. I think 2/5 stars is fair, because it's not complete trash (other than Margaret Qualley's accent), but for me, I don't even think the film is okay. Would have been lower than 2 stars if the film was your typical 100-120 minutes. Disappointing first solo effort from Ethan Coen for me.

I don't go into a movie with expectations.  I don't care that it was made by a Coen brother. I analyze films on their own merit. This one just isn't as good it could have been.

Joel and Ethan really couldn't have gone in more opposite directions with their first solo efforts. The only previous Coens thing it reminded me of was maybe 1985's loopy Crime Wave, which they wrote for Sam Raimi right after Blood Simple. 

I wasn't really into it at the beginning, finding it too juvenile for my taste. The film school scene transitions were pretty grating. I did like Geraldine Viswanathan's performance quite a bit even from the first scenes though, and wasn't familiar with her before this movie. 

I did warm to it by the end. Like another commenter, I found Qualley annoying at first but it felt like part of her character trajectory was going from someone who puts on a front to someone who reveals her true self. Beanie Feldstein killed every scene she was in. Bill Camp and C.J. Wilson both stood out. 

Wouldn't rush out to the theatre for it, but worth checking out at some point if you're a Coens fan.

I also went into this one more/less blind and thought it was pretty terrible. The comedic timing just felt completely off, and the Texas accent did it no favors. I haven't seen The Ladykillers, so I can't compare, but this was just nowhere near as funny as it thought it was. I'm glad you enjoyed it, but I can't see recommending this for anyone.

I liked it a lot, but I'll say that I think the distinction between those who enjoy it and those who don't is going to come down less to Coen expectations, and more to tolerance for and taste in off-color humor.  Not quite everything landed for me, I felt like some of the B-movie reference in the structure and such were a little rough around the edges, but I liked the characters, I liked their screen chemistry, and I was thoroughly entertained throughout.  

And I think most of my friends probably would hate it.  It's just not within the types of movies they enjoy.

I respect that.

I really enjoyed Margaret Qualley’s performance, but I see how it’s a love it or hate it type performance.

For me the jokes landed. I didn’t think it was going for gut-busting hilarity so much as quirk that crescendos in a grand absurdity. For me what really worked was the Sexploitation bent; I thought the meta structural jokes were funny and I liked how it built to the most ridiculous criminal conspiracy possible.

But yeah, I mostly wrote this post to lower peoples expectations to “cheese-ball B-movie”, which I thought it succeeded as.

> Whether it was on purpose or not (I'm sure some people defending this movie will claim it was intentional), it's still god awful and ruins the film.

It drives me nuts how often people in this sub use that "on purpose" defense to dismiss any criticism of a film they like.  Something that is terrible on purpose is still terrible!
I guess I thought the rough edges were part of the 70’s pastiche and set the tone well. It seems like I’m in the minority of people who thought it was worth their time though.
I think it was rough and goofy on purpose, and I think the Texas lesbian was hammy on purpose. Does that count?

Oh it was definitely intentional toward that goal; I just don't think the movie got enough mileage out of that to quite justify as many of them as are there.  It's not a major misstep or anything, just a small thing that didn't quite land for me.  Overall, I definitely thought it was worth the time.

I take your point. I actually felt the same and caught myself thinking “what the fuck is with these trippy and goofy 70’s transitions” but >!when Miley Cyrus is making a mold out of Matt Damon’s dick and the whole “cocks of the rich and powerful” conspiracy is laid bare, I fell in love with this movie. I thought it really made the lesbian-caper-roadtrip-sexploitation come together into a coherent fart joke, and I was delighted!<

Interesting take because I thought that the cinematography was ok and the editing just really uneven and often too in your face but the acting was really good. I really like Margaret in this, I thought her character was a hilarious over the top... Well. Top. I don't think either characters attraction and development is given enough attention to make the love story super believable, and I'm exactly who you're talking about when you say some will appreciate it just for the lesbian elements. I really enjoyed some scenes with them when the film chose to be coherent. But I also felt like the filmmaking is so in your face it's distracting and the characters are under utilized. (Also I agree people should check out Bottoms it's one of my favorite recent comedies and Charlie XCX did the soundtrack, it's the definition of For The Girls and Gays)

It’s a really fun film that I think is actually highly inaccessible on several levels, unfortunately. 

It’s not very high brow, but ironically it’s also way too high concept to be meaningfully low brow. It has mostly “unlikeable” characters, which people are way too quick to confirm their biases with, in spite of being pretty fleshed out and nuanced, and in turn, likable. 

It’s a film which, in many ways, feels like it’s exactly for me, and I viewed it in the right mindset the first time, but I can totally understand how people are struggling to assess which lens to view it with. Bottoms, to a lesser degree, was like this, but if you got the nonsatirical irony of the film, you got there, and if you didn’t, it was still a fun romp.

I mean, you’re right that some people do say “it’s bad on purpose”, but more often, it’s less that it’s bad on purpose, and more that it’s an intentional choice that clearly does work for some people and is thus not bad at all. Shutter Island is full of continuity errors, but anyone who considers them a flaw should be open to the suggestion that their take is bad.

>if you like silly little movies, I think this one is worth your time

I feel the same way. At no point does the movie expect you to take it seriously. I usually try to avoid falling back on the “Just turn your brain off and have fun” line, but it feels obvious to me that that was the goal Cooke and Coen had in mind. It’s not supposed to be anything more than it is.

I’m a bit biased though, I was an extra in one scene and I’m beyond *thrilled* to have made the final cut 😁

Ethan Coen has been adament that he didn't direct the film alone, he co-directed it with his wife, Tricia Cooke, but due to the same DGA rules that prevented him being credited on earlier Coen brothers films, he is the only credited director.

I think if you turn your brain off, you wouldn’t get how brilliant the final turn is. It reminds me of *Black Dynamite* when you learn that Richard Nixon engineered a malt liquor to shrink black America’s…manhood. It’s smart in an incredibly stupid way.

I agree with you that Margaret’s accent took me out of the suspension of disbelief many times. I can’t decide if I would’ve preferred a more realistic accent or if she just wasn’t a “southern beau” so to speak. it’s a funny characterization on paper but didn’t work for me on the screen.
